title: DWP takes some online services offline after identifying a cyber incident
date_note: The page gives no earlier day than its 27 November publication.
place: United Kingdom (national department; location of the incident not stated)
summary: The DWP said it took some online services offline as a precaution after identifying a cyber incident. LBC reports Pat McFadden called it "a serious cyber incident" and could not yet say the cause; the NCSC is investigating. Geo News reports the Prime Minister's spokesperson said there is no evidence of customer data loss. PA reporting says the data protection watchdog is in contact with the DWP. The DWP says regular payments are not affected.
plain: The DWP has taken some online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident. It says benefit and pension payments are not affected. SOCRadar says Universal Credit sign-in and some online applications were unavailable.
exec: A UK government department has taken some online services offline after a cyber incident; the DWP says regular payments are unaffected, and the PM's spokesperson is reported to say there is no evidence of customer data loss.
action: The DWP advises anyone who cannot reach a service to try again later, and says it will never message people to ask for bank details or to click on links.

validation.note: PA News (via Diss Express and AOL/Evening Standard) and EFE (via ABC Color) are separate agencies; each reports the DWP saying it suspended some online services after a cyber incident and that regular payments are unaffected. The DWP page itself was not read.
